newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Strong offshore units help ANZ profit.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Strong offshore units help ANZ profit.

text.p: The Australia and New Zealand Banking Group said on Wednesday its six percent rise in net profit for 1995/96 to A$1.116 billion was due in large part to a fall in its provision for doubtful debts and a strong performance from its overseas divisions.
ANZ said its operating profit before debt provisions from its Australian operations actually fell four percent to A$1.016 billion in 1995/96 from A$1.055 billion in 1994/95.
ANZ Chairman Charles Goode said in a statement with the results that it was a good profit result for shareholders.
"It was built around continued business growth across all sectors, particularly the international operations," Goode said.

"A lower charge for bad debts and growth in non-interest income together with a lower effective tax rate contributed to a strong second half result that was a little ahead of our expectations," he said.
Net profit, after provisioning, from international operations grew 17 percent compared with seven percent in Australia and a decline of five percent from New Zealand.

"Our international operations have contributed strongly to the group result ... In particular our investment banking operations in London performed very strongly in the second half of the year," Goode said.
Chief executive officer Don Mercer said ANZ's total assets grew 13 percent, with reasonable growth across all markets.

ANZ's net profit rose to A$596 million in the second half from A$520 million in the first half, giving the total A$1.116 billion profit. Analysts had on average forecast net profit before abnormals of A$1.05 billion. There were no abnormals.
Total provisions for doubtful debts fell to A$154 million in the 1995/96 year from A$174 million the previous year.
But the provisions fell sharply in the second half to A$52 million from A$102 million in the first half.
"In Australia and New Zealand, gross interest spreads were lower reflecting intensely competitive market conditions, particularly in the home loan market," Mercer said.
"In our international operations, spreads were steady."
Mercer said higher personnel costs were the main factor in the rise in operating expenses to A$3.64 billion from A$3.33 billion the previous year.
Personnel expenses rose to A$1.86 billion for the year from A$1.62 billion while other expenses such as premises expenses and computer expenses were either flat or slightly lower.
"Additional staff were employed in Australia as we centralised back office functions and introduced new technology, the benefits from which will be seen from 1997," Mercer said.

"Also behind the higher personnel expenses were salary increases flowing from the enterprise bargaining agreement, the move to total employment cost packaging for managerial staff, performance related payments and redeployment and retrenchment costs," he said.
Employee numbers rose to 39,721 at September 30 from 39,240 a year earlier.
The operating expenses to net operating income ratio rose to 70.7 percent from 67.7 percent a year earlier.
ANZ shares were up 21 cents at A$7.72 at 2.50 p.m. (0350 GMT). -- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 373-1800
